Bounds 20 to 400 TBq/(GW a) pending better data.

proposed_method: Ash Cs-137 = fuel Cs-137 x ash concentration factor (ash 14-370x wood, S0514; about 90x, S0515 Sweden; peat ash about 20x peat, S0519). Fuel Cs-137 from deposition (Task 1.7 fallout baseline) x soil-to-wood transfer. Measured ash: Sweden 1997 houses 2-21 kBq/kg (S0515); Swedish peat ash 43-34,480 Bq/kg, mean 10,000 (1986-89), reference 1,000 normal and 10,000 high (S0519); Lithuania 2010 up to 7,201 (Lithuanian fuel), 9,800 (Ukrainian pellets) (S0514); US weapons-fallout wood ash 2.9-780 Bq/kg (S0520, 1989-92 survey).
notes: Cs-137 absent before 1945; pre-1950 residue is zero for Cs-137 (inference from fallout history). Weapons-fallout era 1950s-1980s: only one US survey (1992) located; modelled from deposition.

proposed_method: Liberated (air_stack) = Cs-137 in fuel x volatilised fraction f_v. Only an assumption found: about 10% of fuel Cs-137 to flue gas (S0515, citing larger-plant studies, not measured); S0519 states Cs, Pb-210 and Po-210 partly volatilise and condense on fine fly ash, with 99% dust control in the UNSCEAR peat case. Propose f_v central 0.10, bounds 0.02-0.3 (modelled), times (1 - filter efficiency) for stack escape; fly ash capture is impounded/dispersed.
notes: No direct stack measurement found. Stack release = f_v x (1 - dust-control efficiency); the bulk volatilised Cs is captured on fly ash.
